scoringRotation.newGroundRule: FLOW-WEIGHTED (captain decision 399a): the cap goes where a visit covers the most windows it has not already covered — launch flow times time waited, capped at the per-visit window cap — and never-scored first, least-recently-scored breaking ties. Recency alone gave every survivor the same number of visits whatever its tempo, which stranded the tail.
scoringRotation.reproducibility: ROTATION STATE IS COMMITTED EVIDENCE: this run spent its scoring cap where a visit covers the most NEW GROUND — remaining unharvested launch flow, saturating at the per-visit window cap, with least-recently-scored breaking ties — so its output depends on every run before it. The run record names the state it read (path, schema version, SHA-256 before and after) and carries the whole ranked order with the flow term on every row, so the selection is re-derivable from committed artefacts alone — rotation.mjs -> verifySelection.

$comment: Keyed, MadeOnSol, one request per candidate. A GATE, not a score: it asks whether a
deployer is competent, which is necessary and nowhere near sufficient. Stage 0 demonstrates
the gap empirically — it shows the gate PASSING the one deployer we know is not worth the
time.
ON THE VENDOR READING — the MadeOnSol profile leg, which is what --ownership-only runs and
feed.mjs grade on — the denominator is `profile.pump_tokens[].complete` and nothing else.
Never `bonding_rate`, `total_bonded`, `total_tokens_deployed`, `recent_bond_rate`,
`recent_outcomes` or `best_token_peak_mc`, which are trailing windows or stale; and never
/deployer-hunter/{wallet}/tokens, which is bonded-only and so has no denominator at all.
THAT SENTENCE IS SCOPED TO THAT LEG AND IS NOT WHAT THE GATE READS BY DEFAULT (captain
decision 238a narrows it rather than deleting it: it was written about the vendor leg, it
remains true of the vendor leg, and it was only ever unlabelled). screen.mjs gates on the
CREATION-DERIVED MERGED HISTORY, whose completion flags come from the chain's own
bonding-curve state (creation.mjs -> mergeHistories, counted as `bondedFromCurve`) for
launches the vendor page never lists, with the listing's own flag only as the fallback where
the curve went unread. `justification.minCompletionRate` names the reading each bar is
measured on and owns that distinction — read it before quoting this paragraph as the gate's
source.

justification.completionRateSource: NOT A THRESHOLD — the field the other three bars are computed from ON THE VENDOR READING, and the reasoning for it is this block's $comment at length: profile.pump_tokens[].complete agreed with our tape 67/67 on the completion flag with no in-window launch missing, while every published aggregate is a trailing ~7.5-day window their own alert text calls 'lifetime', and /deployer-hunter/{wallet}/tokens is bonded-only and so has no denominator at all. NAME THE LEG, THOUGH (captain decision 238a, which moves no value): that is the leg --ownership-only runs and feed.mjs grade on, and it is NOT screen.mjs's default. By default the three bars are computed over the creation-derived merged history instead, whose completion flags come from the chain's own bonding-curve state (creation.mjs -> mergeHistories, `bondedFromCurve`) for launches this field never lists — so this entry is the anchor for the vendor leg's denominator and not a statement that every gate reading uses it. `justification.minCompletionRate` names the reading each bar is measured on; `justification.minTokens` does the same for the count. Named here as well because this file's contract is that the anchor is in `justification`. AND SINCE CAPTAIN DECISION 351 (2026-08-07) NEITHER LEG'S DENOMINATOR IS THE WHOLE HISTORY: a launch carrying pump.fun's `is_mayhem_mode` is excluded from both sides of the rate, because a mayhem graduation raises a median 0.291 SOL against 85.005 for a classic curve one and so is not competence evidence. THAT CHANGES THE VENDOR LEG BY NOTHING, and it is worth saying why: `profile.pump_tokens` carries no such column, so every launch on that leg is UNREADABLE for the flag and is kept — the same rule the creation-derived leg applies to its own pre-`pump_evt_createevent` launches, not an exemption for this one. `justification.minCompletionRate` owns the argument and the unreadable-flag decision. AND SINCE CAPTAIN DECISION 352b (2026-08-09) THE EVENT IT COUNTS IS RAISE-85 RATHER THAN pump.fun's OWN GRADUATION: net quote inflow into a token's own primary market reaching 85 SOL-equivalent over its first 24 hours, on every venue including pump.fun. `profile.pump_tokens[].complete` is still the field this leg READS, and that is the point worth being precise about — it is no longer the DEFINITION, it is an ESTIMATOR of the definition, and `measure.mjs` → `PUMPFUN_GRADUATION_ESTIMATOR` owns what it is worth in each direction (its negative is exact, since every token that reached 85 SOL graduated; its positive is an upper bound, since 0.82% of graduations did not reach it). So a rate on this leg is an UPPER BOUND on the RAISE-85 rate and errs towards acceptance, and the candidate row's `competenceCriterionEstimated` says how much of it rests on the estimator. ONE THING DID MOVE ON THIS LEG: a `complete` field that is missing or malformed used to read `false` — a vendor schema change would have driven every rate here to 0.0000 with nothing saying so — and is UNREADABLE now, which leaves the launch out of both sides and counts it in `competenceCriterionUnreadable`.
justification.minTokens: MadeOnSol's own spec tells consumers to gate on labeled_tokens >= 3. That is far too low: on our subject deployer a 22-token window read 0.6818 against a true 0.4310, so a window of ~22 was enough to be wrong by 58% relative. 25 is the floor at which their sliding-window artefact stops being the whole measurement, and it is 8x their published gate. NAME THE POPULATION, THOUGH: that evidence is about the VENDOR'S TRAILING WINDOW, while rank.mjs compares `completion.tokens` of whatever history reading the run produced — by default the creation-derived merged listing, which is larger and therefore easier to clear than the window this figure was measured on. The bar is a 'worth scoring at all' filter rather than a claim about the deployer, so the mismatch is bounded, but the two are not the same count and no measurement fixes 25 against the merged one. It is NOT enough for a lifetime claim, which is why the span is reported alongside and why long-horizon consistency is reported UNMEASURED. AND SINCE CAPTAIN DECISION 351 (2026-08-07) `completion.tokens` IS THE NON-MAYHEM COUNT — a third population again, and narrower than the merged listing this paragraph already disclaims. That is on purpose rather than a side effect: `tokens`, `rate` and `spanDays` are three statements about ONE sample, and a sample-size bar read over a wider set than the rate it guards would be the same 'two quantities through one number' defect 351 exists to remove. NO MEASUREMENT FIXES 25 AGAINST THE NON-MAYHEM COUNT EITHER, and for a mayhem-heavy wallet the change runs towards rejection — which is why a shortfall the exclusion caused SAYS SO in rank.mjs → applyGate's own sentence, and why a wallet left with no non-mayhem launch at all is unmeasured rather than rejected. Sizing this bar against the post-351 population is `slot-zero-rederive-gate-population-post-351`, a separate lane, and not this entry's to guess. CAPTAIN DECISION 352b NARROWS THIS COUNT AGAIN AND MOVES NO VALUE: `completion.tokens` is now the launches that survived the mayhem exclusion AND on which the RAISE-85 criterion could be READ, which is a FOURTH population from the three above, and the two exclusions are counted apart on the candidate row rather than merged. The direction is 351's — towards rejection for a wallet whose launches cannot be read — and it is answered the same way: a shortfall the criterion caused SAYS SO in rank.mjs → applyGate's own sentence, and a wallet ANY of whose launches the criterion could not be read on is gate-unmeasured rather than rejected (rank.mjs → `competenceEmptiedByCriterion` where the reading holds nothing at all, `competenceCriterionIncomplete` where it still holds launches — this bar and minSpanDays are exactly why the partial case has to be unmeasured too, since the unreadable launches leave the COUNT as well as the rate), because that shortfall is OUR coverage and not the deployer's record. Sizing 25 against the post-352b population is `slot-zero-rederive-gate-population-post-351` and not this entry's to guess.
justification.minCompletionRate: 0.25, HELD BY CAPTAIN DECISION 231a (2026-08-04), WHICH MOVES NO VALUE AND REWRITES THIS ENTRY: the defect was that the earlier text named NO READING, which made the number unauditable — a completion rate is not one quantity here and the two the tool computes differ by an order of magnitude on the same wallets. NAME THE READING FIRST. This bar is compared against the CREATION-DERIVED MERGED HISTORY that screen.mjs gates on by default — which mints the wallet CREATED, `historySource: "creation-derived"`, the default since record schema 4 with --ownership-only as the opt-out, and the reading of every candidate in the last real run (`runs/2026-08-04.json`, schema 12, 82 candidates, 82 of 82 creation-derived). That reading's median window on those candidates is 147.1 days and its median token count 1,386, and it is the WHOLE creation history for 57 of the 82 (`creation.wholeHistory`). THE VENDOR 70-RECORD PAGE IS A DIFFERENT AND SHORTER QUANTITY AND THIS BAR IS NOT MEASURED ON IT: median span 3.4 days on the same 82 wallets, page-capped at 70 records on 63 of them, and SUCCESS-BIASED rather than merely short, because ownership is a sellable position and the ones worth handing on are the winners — `yHCxHBEa…` shows 280 of the 749 mints it created and so reads 1.0000 on the page against 0.3071 on the gate reading. --ownership-only runs and feed.mjs read that page (FEED.md, 'Why the gate here reads ownership'), so the feed ledger's `completionRate` is not this quantity and a bar argued on one does not transfer to the other. WHAT FIXES THE VALUE, in order of weight. (1) THE CONTROL IS A HARD CEILING. `7ufmve7Z…` — the known-competent operator Stage 0 requires this gate to PASS — reads 0.4325 (109 of 252) on the gate reading, so ANY BAR ABOVE 0.4325 EXCLUDES A WALLET WE KNOW IS GOOD; and its own month-to-month rates span 0.256 (0.381, 0.354, 0.610, 0.375, 0.548, 0.429), so anything above ~0.35 puts it within one ordinary month of exclusion. Its committed-tape lifetime rate, 0.4310 over 239 launches and 103 bonded, is the same ceiling read off this repo's own primary record. (2) WHAT THE BAR DOES ON THE SCREEN'S OWN POPULATION, re-derivable offline from the committed record: over the 66 of that run's 82 candidates that clear minTokens and minSpanDays the median rate is 0.0187, 4 clear 0.25, only 2 clear 0.35, and 0.60 admits NOBODY — a bar that empties the run has spent the keyed allowance to produce no Stage 2 population at all. (3) THE REGIME ARTEFACT READS HIGHER THAN THE CONTROL ON THE VENDOR PAGE — AND THE ASYMMETRY REVERSES ON THE GATE READING, WHICH IS THE ONE THIS BAR IS COMPARED AGAINST. CAPTAIN DECISION 263b (2026-08-05) CORRECTS THIS ENTRY AND MOVES NO VALUE; the defect it fixes is that the earlier text quoted the artefacts on the VENDOR PAGE and the control on BOTH readings inside one sentence, then drew a conclusion that is true of neither reading on its own. TAKE THEM APART. ON THE VENDOR 70-RECORD PAGE the two wallets whose rates are a post-break short-window artefact read 1.0000 (`yHCxHBEa…`, old-regime record 0.1369) and 0.9429 (`GeBJSHK4…`, old-regime record 0.0462) against the control's 0.5429, so on that page there is indeed no bar that removes the two and keeps the control, and raising a bar measured THERE would remove the operator and keep the artefacts. ON THE GATE READING the same three wallets read 0.3089, 0.3303 and 0.4325, so THE ORDER INVERTS AND A BAR IN (0.3303, 0.4325] WOULD REMOVE BOTH ARTEFACTS AND KEEP THE CONTROL (`runs/2026-08-05-seed-comparison.md`, which measured all three the same day; the artefact gate readings are its contribution, the control's 0.4325 is §6 of `slot-zero-gate-bar-measure-own-population`, held in firstmate's records and not in this repo). THE MECHANISM IS THE DENOMINATOR, which is why the inversion is not a fluke of two wallets: the artefacts' page readings are computed over 70 records of a 751-creation and a 327-creation history, and the creation-derived denominator is what collapses 1.0000 to 0.3089. WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT LICENSE. It does not move this bar and 263b explicitly does not: the evidence is n = 2 ARTEFACTS AND ONE CONTROL, ON ONE DAY, with the control's figure taken from one leg and the artefacts' from another about an hour apart; and a band whose lower edge is 0.3303 sits 0.1022 below a control whose own month-to-month rates span 0.256 — so an ordinary month for `7ufmve7Z…` could put it inside the band the artefacts were supposed to occupy, and the separation would vanish with nothing in a run saying so. It is recorded here because 231a's rule is that a bar names the reading it is measured on, and the old sentence's claim ('there is no bar') was a claim about the wrong reading; leaving that uncorrected while the finding existed is the same defect one level in. WHAT WOULD JUSTIFY ACTING ON IT: the same three-way comparison over enough artefacts and controls to say whether the inversion is a property of the readings or of these two wallets, plus a re-read across months rather than on one day. Until then what distinguishes an artefact from an operator is window length and reading, not rate, so the instrument remains an evidence-window rule or the reading itself — and this bar stays at 0.25. (4) THE ASYMMETRY THAT DECIDES WHERE IN THE 0.25–0.35 BAND TO SIT, and it points DOWN. A false REJECTION here is permanent and invisible: the wallet is graded, filed in feed/ledger.json and never offered again (ledger.mjs; the feed never re-polls a wallet already graded). A false ACCEPTANCE is visible and cheap: it costs Stage 2 keyless requests and is then refused by stage2_entry.minRoomLeft — which is exactly what Stage 0 demonstrates on every run, passing `7ufmve7Z…` on this gate and refusing it on room. This gate is 'necessary and nowhere near sufficient' (this block's $comment), so it is deliberately set to fail towards acceptance. 0.25 is also MadeOnSol's own published 'good'-tier bar, which is where the number came from; it is not what holds it now. PROVENANCE, AND IT IS SPLIT BECAUSE THE TWO HALVES ARE AUDITED DIFFERENTLY. FROM THE COMMITTED `runs/2026-08-04.json`, re-derivable offline with no vendor call: the 82-candidate figures (82 of 82 creation-derived, median gate-reading window 147.1 days, median 1,386 tokens, whole creation history on 57 of 82, vendor median span 3.4 days, vendor page capped at 70 records on 63 of 82), the 66-candidate sweep (median 0.0187, 4 clear 0.25, 2 clear 0.35, none clears 0.60), and `yHCxHBEa…`'s page-against-gate pair (1.0000 on the vendor page against 0.3071 on the gate reading, 280 of the 749 mints its ownership listing shows). FROM `slot-zero-gate-bar-measure-own-population` (held in firstmate's records, not in this repo), because these do NOT reproduce from that run record: the control `7ufmve7Z…`'s 0.4325 gate reading, its 0.5429 vendor-page reading and its 0.256 month-to-month range are §6; `GeBJSHK4…`'s 0.9429 is §4.2's live re-read of 2026-08-05, and its §0 summary quotes the same figure; the old-regime records 0.1369 (`yHCxHBEa…`) and 0.0462 (`GeBJSHK4…`) are §0 and §4.2; and the argument itself — the ceiling, the sweep's reading, the artefact comparison and the asymmetry — is §6, §6b, §7 and §8. AND THE VENDOR 70-RECORD PAGE SLIDES, so two snapshots of one wallet days apart legitimately differ and neither is stale: `GeBJSHK4…` reads 0.9429 on that 2026-08-05 re-read and 0.957143 in this repo's own committed `runs/2026-07-29-elite.json` and `feed/ledger.json`, one launch apart on a 70-record window — that gap is a property of the surface, and it is itself part of why this bar is measured on the creation-derived reading rather than on the page. That report's §8 recommends the 0.25–0.35 band and does not choose within it; 231a chooses 0.25 and changes nothing about what the screen admits. ONE CORRECTION TO IT MADE HERE RATHER THAN INHERITED: it dates the creation-derived default to 'schema 12', which is the SCHEMA OF THE RUN IT MEASURED — the default arrived at record schema 4. CAPTAIN DECISION 351 (2026-08-07) NARROWS THE READING THIS BAR IS MEASURED ON, AND MOVES NO VALUE. A mayhem-mode graduation is not competence evidence — measured in `slot-zero-offlaunchpad-graduation-criterion` → `report.md` §4 and §8.2 (held in firstmate's records, not in this repo): a mayhem graduation is preceded by a median net quote inflow of 0.291 SOL into the token's own primary market against 85.005 SOL for a classic curve graduation — 292x cheaper, and not separable in trade data from a token that churned about $1,700 and died — while in 2026-07 mayhem was 27.15% of pump.fun launches and 46.41% of its graduations. So this bar had been measuring two very different achievements through one number, and nearly half of what it counted was the cheap one. IT IS NOW MEASURED ON THE NON-MAYHEM SLICE OF THE CREATION-DERIVED MERGED HISTORY: `measure.mjs` → `measureCompletion` drops a launch whose `is_mayhem_mode` reads true from the NUMERATOR AND THE DENOMINATOR, and rank.mjs compares `completion.rate` over what is left. THE DENOMINATOR HALF IS NOT OPTIONAL: a numerator-only exclusion drives a mayhem-heavy deployer's rate towards 0.0000 and removes them from the gate, which is captain decision 227c — excluding mayhem-heavy deployers outright — and 227c is NOT reversed and REMAINS DECLINED. WHAT THIS DOES TO 0.25 IS UNMEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT GUESSED AT HERE: every figure in the paragraphs above — the control's 0.4325, the 66-candidate sweep's 0.0187 median, the artefacts' 0.3089 and 0.3303 — is a PRE-351 reading over pooled mayhem and non-mayhem launches, and none has been re-derived on the new one. Re-deriving them, and the 112 all-time gate-passers, the 58 active in July and the monthly denominators that rest on the same pooling, is `slot-zero-rederive-gate-population-post-351` and is a separate lane; the value stays 0.25 until it reports, because moving a bar and changing what it measures in one step leaves neither auditable. THE ASYMMETRY IN (4) IS WHY WAITING IS SAFE: this bar is deliberately set to fail towards acceptance, and every figure above was measured on a denominator that INCLUDED mayhem launches, so what the narrowing removes is a deployer whose mayhem graduations were inflating their rate — visibly, and then refused at Stage 2 — while a deployer with no mayhem record reads exactly what they read before. AN UNREADABLE FLAG IS KEPT IN THIS DENOMINATOR AND COUNTED: `is_mayhem_mode` is a column on Dune's `pump_evt_createevent` and on no other surface this tool reads, so the creation walk, `pump_call_create` rows and the ownership listing all supply launches with nothing to read. Dropping those would empty this bar's denominator for every walk-sourced candidate on evidence about the SURFACE rather than about the deployer — the permanent, invisible direction — so they stay in, and the run record's `competenceMayhemUnreadable` (record schema 19; equal to `tokens` AND `competenceMayhemExcluded` 0, i.e. the pre-351 reading — both conjuncts, since a candidate can have launches excluded and still have nothing readable left among the rest) is what makes the choice auditable per candidate. A deployer left with NO non-mayhem launch is UNMEASURED rather than failed (rank.mjs → `competenceEmptiedByMayhem`): zero of zero is an absent measurement and not a rate of 0. CAPTAIN DECISION 352b (2026-08-09) CHANGES WHAT THIS BAR COUNTS AS A COMPLETION, AND MOVES NO VALUE. The measure is RAISE-85 — net quote inflow into a token's own primary market reaching 85 SOL-equivalent over its first 24 hours — on every venue including pump.fun, replacing pump.fun's own graduation flag as the DEFINITION. The 85 was read off the data rather than fitted (graduating non-mayhem tokens read 85.005 SOL at p50 AND p99 over 157,259 launches) and has ZERO token-level false positives against 108,310 non-graduating tokens, so a rate computed from it is a LOWER BOUND: measured over 176,200 July-active deployers it PROMOTED ZERO deployers over this bar at every launch-count floor and demoted 1,417. THE BAR IS NOT TO BE LOWERED TO BUY RECALL — at 50 SOL the zero-false-positive property is already gone (42 promotions) and the one-directional safety argument goes with it. THE ORDER OF THE TWO EXCLUSIONS IS LOAD-BEARING: RAISE-85 as a definition only touches the NUMERATOR, since it never registers a mayhem graduation, so had mayhem LAUNCHES stayed in this denominator a mayhem-heavy deployer would run to 0.0000 and be dropped — which is captain decision 227c, and 227c REMAINS DECLINED. The mayhem exclusion therefore runs FIRST over the whole history and the criterion only over what it leaves. A LAUNCH THE CRITERION CANNOT BE READ ON LEAVES BOTH SIDES AND IS NEVER SCORED AS A FAILURE (`competenceCriterionUnreadable`, record schema 21), and a deployer ANY of whose launches could not be read is UNMEASURED rather than failed — not only one left with none readable, because those launches leave `tokens` and `spanDays` as well as the rate and minTokens/minSpanDays would otherwise reject a wallet over OUR coverage (rank.mjs → `competenceCriterionIncomplete`). WHAT THIS BAR IS COMPARED AGAINST TODAY IS AN UPPER BOUND ON THE RAISE-85 RATE: every route this repo has reads the criterion through pump.fun's graduation flag, whose negative is exact and whose positive is 0.82% generous, so the reading errs towards ACCEPTANCE — the direction (4) above says this bar is deliberately set to fail in — and `competenceCriterionEstimated` says how much of a given rate rests on it. WHAT 352b DOES NOT ESTABLISH: equivalent strictness across venues. The same 85-SOL bar is reached by 0.80% of new pump.fun tokens against 0.25% on Meteora DBC and 46.71% on Meteora CPAMM; `slot-zero-cross-venue-strictness-measure` owns that question (held in firstmate's records, not in this repo) and NO CLAIM OF CROSS-VENUE COMPARABILITY MAY BE READ OFF THIS ENTRY. AND EVERY FIGURE ABOVE REMAINS A PRE-351, PRE-352b POOLED READING — the control's 0.4325, the 66-candidate sweep's 0.0187 median, the artefacts' 0.3089 and 0.3303 — none of them re-derived on this measure. That is `slot-zero-rederive-gate-population-post-351`, which runs AFTER 352b and must re-derive under the measure as adopted here; the value stays 0.25 until it reports, for the reason the 351 paragraph above already gives.
justification.minSpanDays: A high rate earned inside a single day is a burst, not a record — and this bar measures exactly that: rank.mjs compares `completion.spanDays`, which is FIRST DEPLOY TO LAST DEPLOY over the gate's history reading, not time-to-bond. The two are not the same quantity and an earlier version of this entry justified the first with a distribution of the second, computed from `curve_last_tx_s`; that column is formally ruled a valid upper BOUND and not a usable timing (population-tape-2026-07-29/IMPORT.md, Corrections 4, median overshoot 8.85x), so the clause is withdrawn rather than re-derived and the column is not quoted here. The measured median graduation time on this operator is 1,042 s = 17.4 MINUTES (IMPORT.md, Corrections 5), so 14 days is orders of magnitude above what a launch needs to resolve: this bar exists to refuse a wallet whose whole history is one burst, not to wait for bonding. NOTE THE RESIDUAL GAP, which no span bar closes: a wallet that deploys most of its tokens in the last 48 hours of a 14-day span still clears this, and its unresolved launches then depress its completion rate — which errs towards rejection, the direction this tool prefers to fail in. AND SINCE CAPTAIN DECISION 351 (2026-08-07) 'the gate's history reading' IS THE NON-MAYHEM SLICE OF IT: `completion.spanDays` is first deploy to last deploy over the launches that survived the mayhem exclusion, not over the whole history — a THIRD quantity from the two this entry already keeps apart. It is the coherent reading rather than a widening, because the rate this bar guards is now the non-mayhem rate, so 'was that rate earned inside a burst' is a question about the non-mayhem launches. Nothing measured says how often a mayhem-heavy wallet's non-mayhem launches are burst-shaped; the value does not move for it, and the population re-derivation is `slot-zero-rederive-gate-population-post-351`. CAPTAIN DECISION 352b NARROWS IT ONCE MORE AND MOVES NO VALUE: `completion.spanDays` is first deploy to last deploy over the launches that survived the mayhem exclusion AND on which RAISE-85 could be read — a FOURTH quantity. Coherent for the same reason as before rather than a widening: the rate this bar guards is computed over exactly that set, and a span measured over a wider one would be the 'two quantities through one number' defect these entries exist to remove. Nothing measured says how often the unreadable launches are burst-shaped; the value does not move for it.

$comment: ACTIVE. This is the `stage2_seam` block of thresholds v2.0.0, promoted in place — the two
values it reserved were pinned by the stage-0/1 lane BEFORE this lane existed to apply them,
and they are carried over unchanged with their original justification. That ordering is the
audit trail and it is the reason the block was not rewritten: a bar derived after seeing the
output it judges is not a bar. See git history for the superseded block verbatim.
What Stage 2 answers, from the captain's brief verbatim: 'Can I beat the dev and all other
wallets sniping the same tokens created by the dev currently?' — the ENTRY half of it.
(1) ENTRY ROOM: how much of the opening window the dev and its own cohort take before an
outsider is filled. The method of slot-zero-june-regime-change/report.md 5.1, 'the
operation's share of the curve's bottom'. In the captain's own framing, which is the
one the docs keep: this measures HOW BADLY CONFIGURED THE DEV'S OWN LAUNCH BOT IS.
(2) THE FIELD: what every OTHER sniping wallet on those same tokens achieved — fill, queue
position, and realised P&L. The question is whether WE beat them, so the competition is
measured and never assumed.
Both are keyless, from pump.fun fills. Stage 2 spends NO keyed request: it reuses the mint
list from the profile Stage 1 already fetched.
REPORTED AS DISTRIBUTIONS PLUS A HIT RATE, NEVER A MEAN. A standing captain bar for this
class of claim. Sniper outcomes are heavy-tailed on both sides, so a mean describes nobody.
NOT SCORED HERE, AND NO EXIT SIGNAL MAY REACH AN ENTRY NUMBER: exit feasibility (when the dev
sells relative to mint and to outsider inflow, whether the trigger is a SIZE and therefore
caps our position because our own buy counts towards it, and whether an outsider could have
exited first) is stage 3's separate deliverable. The prediction-grading loop is another lane
again. Room to enter is not room to leave, and one blended number cannot be read back apart.

justification.minRoomLeft: CARRIED UNCHANGED from thresholds v2.0.0 `stage2_seam.reservedMinRoomLeft`, pinned before this lane existed. Anchored on the only regime this project has MEASURED as profitable for create-slot outsiders. June report 5.1 puts the operation's share of the curve's bottom at 0.451 before 2026-06-04 (room 0.549) and PRINTS 0.768 after (room 0.232) — but that cell is quoted here as the PUBLISHED FIGURE, not as a measurement: it is the rank-43/44 order statistic of its own 89-launch series, whose median is 0.771 (room 0.229), and 0.771 is what this repo pins (captain decision 135c; the decomposition is in population-tape-2026-07-29/IMPORT.md -> 'Corrections'). THE UNIT THIS BAR IS COMPARED AGAINST IS THE PER-LAUNCH MEDIAN, not the pooled per-entry one (captain decision 140a): every scored launch contributes its own median entry and exactly one observation, so a launch with dozens of priced entrants cannot outvote a launch with one. entry.mjs computes both — entryCostPerSolStakedByLaunch is what the verdict reads, entryCostPerSolStaked is the finer-grained per-entry evidence reported beside it — and a test pins the gate to the per-launch unit. THE DENOMINATOR IS THE SEAT, NOT THE WHOLE STAKE, and the name understates that: the per-entry ratio is entryCostSol / FieldEntrant.createSlotFillSol — the entrant's own create-slot curve buy — and NOT its whole-window FieldEntrant.stakeSol. On the committed tape the two coincide for the median entrant (stakeSol / createSlotFillSol reads p50 1.000, p90 1.000, max 47.63 over 757 priced entries), and the seat is the smaller denominator, so the implemented ratio is the LARGER one and this bar is the easier one to trip — conservative, which is the direction the cost leg must fail in. A seat priced at 0.12 therefore costs essentially the whole of the gross prize, and since gross is an upper bound the median entrant cannot clear it — that is arithmetic, not a preference. NOTE THE DIRECTION OF THE ERROR: an out-of-transaction landing tip is NOT in the numerator, so the measured price of the seat is a LOWER bound and this bar is harder to trip than the truth warrants. justification.minPricedFraction: 0.8 of the create-slot field must be priced on-chain before any after-cost reading may stand. This is the coverage floor behind rule 1 of the ruling — unmeasured cost is never a pass — and the failure it exists for is specific: the cost walk goes launch by launch under a per-candidate RPC ceiling, so a budget that runs out part-way leaves a cost distribution describing only the launches walked FIRST, which are the newest ones. That is a biased sample rather than a short one, and a biased sample of a cost is a wrong number. 0.8 bounds the unpriced share to a fifth. THE CEILING COSTS WHOLE LAUNCHES AND NEVER HALF OF ONE, and that is enforced at BOTH ends rather than asserted: a launch is not started unless the remaining budget covers its whole target list, and — because that reservation cannot see retries or a re-asked null getTransaction, so the ceiling can still bite mid-walk — a launch that came back short is DISCARDED whole, its partial pricing dropped and the launch counted in entry.coverage.cost.launchesDiscarded (entry.coverage.cost.launchesSkippedForBudget is the other end: launches the reservation never started, on which nothing was spent). Without the second half the bias this bar exists to bound would reappear one level down, inside a launch, where a truncated walk holds the earliest entrants by slot. justification.maxRequestsPerLaunch: MEASURED from the committed tape's own build metadata, and the POPULATION MATTERS because the tape's windows are not all the same length. A live Stage 2 walk always reads a 60s window, and over the 210 committed launches whose stored window_ms is 60000 the pages needed per launch run p50 4, p90 6, p95 6, MAX 13. The pooled figure across all 235 covered launches — p50 4, p90 8, p95 13, MAX 24 — is inflated by the 21 of them taped over 300s (and 4 over 120s), and it is what an earlier version of this entry quoted. The cap is on REQUESTS rather than pages because the endpoint sheds ~24.7% of what it is asked for (51,715 OK against 16,960 HTTP 429 on that same build) and the client retries; counting only successes would let a launch cost 3x the printed plan. At that shed rate a page costs ~1.33 requests, and a page is only STARTED when a whole 3-request page cost still fits (i.e. at spent <= 15), so 18 requests starts ABOUT 11-12 PAGES — not the 13-14 an earlier version claimed, which counted requests the loop will not spend. WHAT THAT COVERS, STATED EXACTLY RATHER THAN ROUNDED UP: 11-12 pages is roughly double the 60s p95 of 6, but it does NOT cover that population's observed maximum of 13 — the 2 launches in 210 (1.0%) that needed 13 pages would be dropped at the mean shed rate. That is the reported failure below, not a silent one, and it is why the value does not move: raising the cap to cover a 1% tail costs the whole 7 x 10 x 18 = 1,260 stage arithmetic (3 x 8 x 18 = 432 before captain decision 190a raised the launch cap, and 3 x 10 x 18 = 540 before the proof-coverage lane raised the scoring cap to 7 on 2026-08-04), and it is under open captain decision 193c besides. THE BOUND IS EXACT RATHER THAN APPROXIMATE: a page can cost up to 3 requests (one attempt plus two backoffs), so the walk reserves the WHOLE per-page cost before starting a page and a launch therefore costs at most 18 and never 20. Checking the cap only between pages would have let a walk with one request of headroom spend three, breaking the stage arithmetic the dry run prints as the entire exposure. THE TAIL IS DROPPED, NOT TRUNCATED SILENTLY: a launch that spends the cap without reaching the mint is reported as DROPPED with its own note, and the sampling bias is stated because the launches too busy to walk are exactly the interesting ones.

(i) LIVE: at 2000ms two consecutive Stage 2 runs against swap-api each lost 4 of the subject's 8 launches to HTTP 429 after all three attempts, so the run reported `entry-unmeasured` where the truth is `entry-room-absent`; the same code at 7000ms walked all 8 and produced `entry-room-absent`. A fast wrong answer is worth nothing, and the failure is silent in the direction that matters — a dropped launch degrades the verdict rather than announcing the pacing is wrong. (ii) THE TAPE BUILDER'S OWN RECORD against this same endpoint: the committed `window/*.meta.json` `delay` field — the adaptive delay each build settled on — reads p50 4.92s, p75 15s, p90 15.5s, max 40s, with only p10-p25 near 1.2s; and its shed share by delay quartile is 24.2% / 24.8% / 28.5% / 23.8% over the 238 builds carrying a stats block, i.e. 23.8-28.5% with the SLOWEST quartile no better than the fastest — an earlier version of this entry called that 'flat at ~24-25%', which understates the third quartile by ~4 points without changing what it establishes: backing off does not buy immunity and there is no cheap corner to sit in. 7s is therefore pinned deliberately between that p50 and p75 rather than at the bottom of the range. COST: the request arithmetic is untouched BY THIS PIN — pacing moves wall clock and never exposure — but the wall clock is not, so at the launch cap of 10 captain decision 190a set and the scoring cap of 7 the proof-coverage lane set (7 x 10 x 18 = 1,260) the typical run is about 49 minutes and the worst case about 147, and every printed estimate says so. At the launch cap of 8 this entry was written against the same pacing read about 17 and about 50, and at a scoring cap of 3 against a launch cap of 10 it read about 21 and about 63.
justification.keylessRetryBackoffMs: The tape build shed a quarter of its requests and its own recorded delay ranges from 0.75s to 40s, i.e. it backed off and retried through them. A client that treats a 429 as terminal cannot walk this endpoint at all - the first live check of the pager died on one, three launches in. Two retries at 3s and 9s clear the ordinary case, and EVERY attempt counts against both the per-launch cap and the stage ceiling, so a retry-heavy run gets a dropped launch rather than an unbounded one.
justification.tradePageLimit: 100 is what the trade endpoint serves per page and is the figure the AGENTS.md note is anchored on. Asking for less would multiply the request count for no benefit; the endpoint's own cap is what it is.
justification.windowMs: 60000 is the window_ms of 210 of the committed population tape's 239 launches — its MODAL window and not its only one: 25 were taped over 300000 and 4 over 120000, and calling it 'the tape's window_ms' (as an earlier version of this entry did) hides the 5x builds that inflate every page distribution measured across the whole tape (see maxRequestsPerLaunch). It has NO live use of its own any more: it is a FLOOR inside pumpfun.mjs -> windowReachMs, and nothing else reads it. That one derivation answers BOTH forward-reaching questions ON THE SWAP-API SOURCE — how far the seek cursor must reach past the mint, and whether a launch is old enough to have finished happening — because there they are the same instant. SCOPED RATHER THAN WEAKENED, AND THE SCOPE IS THE CORRECTION: this entry used to state it of Stage 2 flatly, and captain decision 260a's fill-source injection makes eligibility a question asked of the fill source, so 'both questions, one function' is a property of the swap-api source and not of Stage 2 in general. The swap-api derivation and every figure below it are untouched. It does NOT decide which fills are inside the measured window — windowSlotSpan does — because the mint time it would be measured from comes from the vendor and the fills come from pump.fun, and there is nothing to reconcile the two clocks with. HISTORY, read the tense, because this value has been mis-scoped TWICE and the second time is the instructive one. It once decided eligibility alone, so a launch aged 60-65s passed 'old enough to have finished happening' while the newest instant the walk reaches for had not happened yet — the same tail truncation seekMarginMs exists to prevent, arriving from the future side. The fix was the hand-written sum windowMs + seekMarginMs = 65000ms, which was correct only while the seek cursor was ALSO 65000ms and the 160-slot span was reckoned at a nominal 400ms/slot (64.0s). Captain decision 144a moved the cursor to windowReachMs and left that sum behind, and the chain then drifted past the nominal rate unaided: at the measured 446.55ms/slot maximum 160 slots is 71448ms, so the sum ran 6448ms short of the span and 20000ms short of the reach, and a launch could be admitted 20s before the cursor's own bound was in the past. RAISING THE SUM TO 71448 WOULD HAVE RE-ARMED THE IDENTICAL TRAP, because the defect was never the number — it was writing a DURATION for something the chain controls. Both questions derive from windowSlotSpan at a MEASURED worst-case slot rate through the one function, on that source. That rate is a PINNED constant, so the gate moves only when the slot rate is re-measured against a newer committed tape and the pin is raised — what the derivation buys is that a chain slowing past the pin fails the tape-derived guard loudly instead of silently leaving the gate short, and that raising the pin moves the gate and the seek cursor together. Membership stays windowSlotSpan's alone regardless. The old assertion windowSlotSpan x 400ms <= windowMs + seekMarginMs no longer exists — it was denominated in the variable that did not move, so it stayed true and went out of validity with nothing failing. Coverage is now enforced by the describe block 'the seek cursor reaches the whole declared slot window, at a MEASURED slot rate' in test/deployer-screen.test.ts, which re-derives the slot rate from the committed tapes on every run, asserts the reach covers the whole declared span, and asserts the eligibility gate IS that reach — read out of a live scoreCandidateEntry rather than off the source text. Widening the span still fails loudly, through that block.
justification.windowSlotSpan: MEASURED, and deliberately NOT ceil(windowMs/400)=150, which is measurably too narrow. Across the 210 committed launches whose stored window_ms is 60000 the observed slot span is p50 151, p75 153, p90 155, p95 155, MAX 158 — and 51% of them hold at least one fill beyond createSlot+150 (37.1% beyond 151, 5.2% beyond 155, 0.0% beyond 160). This is not a rounding nuisance: the trailing fills are disproportionately LATE SELLS, and dropping one flips a wallet from closed to open, which shrinks fieldClosedRoundTrips — itself a gate at minFieldRoundTrips 10. So a too-narrow span silently changes gate outcomes. 160 covers 100% of observed windows with margin over the observed max of 158. THE OTHER DIRECTION, ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN AS AN OBJECTION: at the tape's observed rate (60s <-> p50 151 slots, ~397ms/slot) 160 slots is ~63.5s, so the live window is up to ~3.5s WIDER than the tape's 60s windows, and the extra late sells make realised P&L read better than the ground-truth recipe would. Because the field leg is veto-only it loosens rather than tightens — a too-generous field can only fail to veto, never earn a verdict — and the magnitude is small. THAT MAGNITUDE CLAIM IS CITED, NOT MEASURED HERE: the figure behind it (the margin sits at the thinnest part of the window, p50 18 / p95 52 fills in the last 5s) is carried over from the PR #7 review comment that recorded this tradeoff, which supplied it without naming a population, and it is reproduced nowhere in this repo — unlike the span figures above, which name theirs (the 210 committed launches whose stored window_ms is 60000). 160 was chosen on measurement, so no change is implied. WHICH OF THE TWO CONVERSIONS OF 160 SLOTS TO READ: the ~63.5s above is the TAPE'S OWN OBSERVED RATE (~397ms/slot, from 60s <-> p50 151 slots) and is SUPERSEDED by the 71448ms figure below, which converts the same 160 slots at the MEASURED WORST-CASE 446.55ms/slot. Both describe the same span and differ only in the rate; the chain's rate rose between them. Re-deriving the ~63.5s conversion and the ~3.5s-wider claim resting on it belongs to A SEPARATE LANE, so the older number is left standing rather than silently updated — read it as history, and read 71448ms as the bound anything in force is measured against. NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH ELIGIBILITY: this span is what decides a launch is old enough to measure, through pumpfun.mjs -> windowReachMs on the swap-api source. AN EARLIER VERSION SAID 'AND NO OTHER ROUTE', AND THAT IS THE ANCHOR THE seekMarginMs AND windowMs ENTRIES ALREADY DROPPED: captain decision 260a's fill-source injection makes eligibility a question asked of whichever fill source Stage 2 was given, so 'no other route' was a claim about one source written as a claim about Stage 2 in general — true when written and stale with nothing failing, which is why none of the three entries names a route any more. THE SPAN'S OWN ROLE IS UNCHANGED and no value moves for this: wherever windowReachMs answers eligibility, this span is what it is derived from, and the test named below reads that out of a live run rather than off any module's source text. HISTORY, and it is worth the tense, because the same claim failed twice here. This entry used to say the eligibility gate DOMINATED the span (160 slots being 64.0s at the nominal 400ms/slot against a 65000ms gate) and that a test pinned windowSlotSpan x 400ms <= windowMs + seekMarginMs. That inequality was DELETED because it was denominated in the variable that did not move: the span never changed, the chain's slot rate did, so it stayed true and went out of validity with nothing failing. Captain decision 144a then scaled the SEEK CURSOR with this span while the eligibility gate stayed a hand-written 65000ms, i.e. 6448ms short of the 71448ms this span is worth at the measured 446.55 ms/slot maximum and 20000ms short of the reach. Both halves now derive from this span at that measured rate, so widening the span widens the reach AND the gate together and neither can outrun it. The enforcement is the describe block 'the seek cursor reaches the whole declared slot window, at a MEASURED slot rate' in test/deployer-screen.test.ts, which re-derives the slot rate from the committed tapes on every run, asserts the reach covers the whole declared span, and asserts the eligibility gate IS that reach. Widening the span still fails loudly, through that block. STAGE 0 DELIBERATELY DOES NOT USE THIS: it measures each committed launch over its own stored window, because the 1,502-pair reproduction against wallet_launch_pnl.csv is computed that way and that regression guard is not traded for cosmetic consistency between the two paths.
justification.seekMarginMs: The walk seeks from createdAtMs + windowReachMs = max(windowMs, ceil(windowSlotSpan x MAX_MS_PER_SLOT)) + this, i.e. 85000ms at the pinned values: a reach derived from the SPAN at a measured worst-case slot rate (MEASURED_MAX_MS_PER_SLOT 446.55 x SLOT_RATE_MARGIN 1.1 -> MAX_MS_PER_SLOT 500), with windowMs surviving there only as a FLOOR. HISTORY: before captain decision 144a the seek was createdAtMs + windowMs + this, and this margin placed the cursor; it no longer does. This margin is added ON TOP of that span-derived reach and keeps its own separate job — clock slack, so a vendor mint time running EARLY by less than 5s cannot cut the tail off the window before the slot trim ever sees it. It replaces a tail-truncation detector that could not discriminate — launches simply stop trading before the nominal window end (p50 observed span 151 against a 160 span), so any such detector fires on nearly every launch and carries no information. Designing the failure out beats reporting it. COST: the walk still pages BACKWARDS to the mint and still trims by slot afterwards, so the margin only adds rows at the newest end — about 5s of trading, roughly 30 fills at a p50 of 362 fills per window over the 210 launches taped at 60s — the population a live walk matches; pooled across all 235 covered launches the p50 is 381 and the answer is the same — i.e. at most one extra page of 100. THAT PARAGRAPH SIZES THE MARGIN ALONE AND IS NO LONGER THE WALK'S COST, which is the span-derived reach's: at 85000ms rather than 65000ms the page cost over the 127 committed launches that can show the effect goes p50 5 / p90 7 / p95 8 / max 14 to p50 6 / p90 8 / p95 9 / max 17, and 4 of 127 = 3.1% now exceed the ~16 pages maxRequestsPerLaunch affords and are dropped as request-cap, where it was 0 of 127. (That is its own measurement over its own named population and is NOT the '1% tail' maxRequestsPerLaunch cites, which is 2 launches in 210 over the 60s-taped population that structurally cannot show this gap. Do not read the two as the same number. pumpfun.mjs -> windowReachMs owns the whole page-cost story and test/deployer-screen.test.ts pins these same figures.) THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE CANDIDATE'S, NOT THE LAUNCH'S, AND THE ZERO-SLACK HALF OF IT IS NOW FIXED (captain decision 190a). When this entry was written minLaunchesSampled and maxLaunchesPerCandidate were the same pinned value (8), so there was no slack — ONE such drop among a candidate's 8 planned launches left 7 sampled and scoreEntry returned entry-unmeasured for the WHOLE CANDIDATE, a naive independent-launches ESTIMATE of 1 - (1 - 4/127)^8 = about 22.6% of candidates. The cap is now 10 against the same floor of 8, so a candidate absorbs TWO drops and the same estimate falls to about 0.32%; maxLaunchesPerCandidate owns that arithmetic and its correlation caveat, and a test pins the figure. The DROP RATE ITSELF IS UNCHANGED — this margin still costs 4 of 127 launches, and that is the number this entry is responsible for. Both estimates take their base rate from ONE deployer's long-window launches, which are also the busiest on the tape. An unmeasured verdict is 'no answer' and never a rejection, and the drop is counted and reported where the truncated tail was silent. The stage arithmetic moved with the caps and not with this margin: 7 x 10 x 18 = 1,260, where it was 3 x 10 x 18 = 540 before the scoring cap went to 7 and 3 x 8 x 18 = 432 before the launch cap went to 10. IT ALSO BOUNDS ELIGIBILITY, because it must, AND THAT IS THE SAME BOUND RATHER THAN A SECOND ONE: a launch is not old enough to measure until the instant the seek cursor reaches for is in the past, so on the swap-api walk the gate IS the reach — 85000ms at the pinned values — and moves with it. NO MODULE AND FUNCTION NAME IS GIVEN FOR THAT GATE ANY MORE, AND THE DELETION IS THE CORRECTION. This entry used to say 'stage2.mjs and bundling.mjs both skip a launch younger than windowReachMs — the identical call'. Captain decision 260a's Stage 2 fill-source injection moves that call: eligibility becomes a question asked of whichever fill source Stage 2 was given, and windowReachMs is what the SWAP-API source answers it with rather than what those two modules call. THE DERIVATION THIS ENTRY OWNS IS UNCHANGED and so is the 85000ms it produces; what changed is that a call site is not a durable anchor for it. A justification anchored on one goes stale with nothing failing — the same defect shape as the windowSlotSpan x 400ms inequality this file records deleting, which stayed true while ceasing to mean anything. What guarantees the gate IS the reach is the test named below, read out of a live scoreCandidateEntry, and that is the thing to check. A launch has finished happening exactly when the instant the cursor seeks to is in the past, so there is nothing left to reconcile. HISTORY: the gate was a hand-written windowMs + seekMarginMs = 65000ms, which held only while the cursor was also 65000ms; captain decision 144a moved the cursor and the chain kept drifting, leaving the gate 6448ms short of the 71448ms the 160-slot span is worth at the measured 446.55 ms/slot maximum and 20000ms short of the reach. It shipped as a knowing residual because the error is one-directional and safe — an early-admitted launch loses its late sells, so its field reads WORSE, and the field leg is veto-only — but it is the class of false rejection that is permanent and invisible, since a graded wallet is filed and never offered again. Raising the constant to 71448 would have re-armed the trap at the next drift; deriving it removes the class. The gate is now asserted, from a live scoreCandidateEntry, by the test 'THE ELIGIBILITY GATE IS THE SAME BOUND, derived' in test/deployer-screen.test.ts. THIS IS A CURSOR HINT AND NOT A TOLERANCE: the pre-mint tripwire still compares ts < createdAtMs with ZERO slack (the measured gap is exactly 0 on all 235 committed launches) and coverage is still discharged only by the endpoint explicitly saying nothing older exists.
justification.maxKeylessRequests: Stage 2's own sub-ceiling, enforced on its own client so it cannot eat the --consistency pass's budget. 7 x 10 x 18 = 1,260 is the exact declared worst case, so no plan-level truncation is possible: the ceiling and the plan agree, and the dry run prints both. It was 432 at a launch cap of 8 and 540 at a scoring cap of 3; captain decision 190a raised the launch cap to 10 for headroom against a dropped launch and the proof-coverage lane raised the scoring cap to 7 on 2026-08-04, and this ceiling moved WITH each of them, because the two being the same number is the property that makes the dry run the whole exposure. Typical cost is far lower - at the measured p50 of 4 pages plus shedding it is about 6 requests a launch, so roughly 420 for a full run. At the pinned 7s pacing for this host that is about 49 minutes typical against about 147 minutes worst case, and the run prints both so an operator does not mistake a slow walk for a hang. A launch is only started when a full per-launch cap of headroom remains, so a run can never abandon a launch half-walked.

$comment: THE PRICE OF THE SEAT. Captain's standing ruling, 2026-08-02: fees are part of the entry
window, and 'enterable' means enterable AFTER what it costs to enter. Captain decision 136b
adds the field's AFTER-COST result, which is what stops the field leg being veto-only.
Keyless, and it spends NO vendor quota — it is Solana RPC, on the same host and the same
pacing as the creation walk. It spends no swap-api request either: every signature it prices
came free with a fill Stage 2 had already parsed.
IT RUNS ONLY WHEN THE FREE LEGS HAVE NOT ALREADY REFUSED. Room and the gross field are
arithmetic over fills in hand, so they are scored first; a deployer that fails either costs
zero RPC requests. That ordering is the whole cost model.
WHAT IT CANNOT SEE, and it must travel with every number this block produces: a landing tip
paid in a SEPARATE transaction of the same bundle is not recoverable from the entrant's own
transaction and is not measured anywhere in this repo's ground truth either. Its absence
biases the answer OPTIMISTICALLY — entry looks cheaper, and the field more profitable, than
either was. So the cost leg is a GATE and never a pass.

justification.maxRpcRequestsPerCandidate: 500 SINCE CAPTAIN DECISION 197b (2026-08-04), AND WHAT IT IS SIZED AGAINST IS PER-LAUNCH HEADROOM RATHER THAN A TOTAL: 500 / maxLaunchesPerCandidate 10 = 400 / 8 = 50 union transactions a launch, so captain decision 190a's launch-cap raise leaves the cost leg exactly the room it had before it. THE MEASUREMENT UNDER IT IS UNCHANGED and is still the committed tape's, re-derived 2026-08-02 rather than copied. Distinct transactions per launch, over the 235 covered launches: the create-slot scope reads p50 7, p90 13, MAX 20 (post-break p50 7, p90 12, max 14); the whole-window scope over CLOSED create-slot outsiders reads p50 18, p90 35, MAX 70 (post-break p50 19, p90 28, max 70). The two scopes are UNIONED before anything is fetched, so a closed entrant's create-slot transaction is paid for once, AND THE UNION IS WHAT MUST BE COSTED: re-running entryCostTargets as the code calls it over those 235 launches gives p50 19, p90 35, p95 41, MAX 74 distinct transactions per launch — not 7 + 18. At maxLaunchesPerCandidate 10 that is about 190 requests at the median, ~350 at p90 and ~740 at the observed worst; at the 8 this entry was first written against it read ~152 / ~280 / ~592. THE INTERACTION THAT MADE THE RAISE NECESSARY, named here because the earlier version of this entry argued only that the median and the p90 still fitted: stage2.mjs skips a WHOLE launch when the remaining per-candidate ceiling cannot cover its target list — a launch is never priced half-way — and entry.mjs then returns entry-cost-unmeasured if the priced share falls below minPricedFraction 0.8. THAT SHARE IS A HIT RATE OVER FIELD ENTRANTS, NOT OVER LAUNCHES (entry.mjs -> entryCostPriced = hitRate(field, e => Number.isFinite(e.entryCostSol))), and a launch skipped for budget is by construction one of the heaviest, so it removes a disproportionate share of the numerator while every one of its entrants stays in the denominator. TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES LIVE IN THIS PARAGRAPH AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER. The first is the PER-PLANNED-LAUNCH HEADROOM, ceiling / maxLaunchesPerCandidate, which is the captain's sizing metric and is held CONSTANT by the raise at 500 / 10 = 400 / 8 = 50 requests a planned launch — that is why 500 and not another number. The second is the BREACH POINT, the sustained per-launch cost at which the priced share first falls under minPricedFraction, which on a LAUNCH-COUNT reading is ceiling / ceil(minPricedFraction x cap): 400 / ceil(0.8 x 8) = 400 / 7 = 57.1 transactions a launch at the old cap of 8, 400 / ceil(0.8 x 10) = 400 / 8 = 50.0 at the cap of 10 with the ceiling left at 400, and 500 / 8 = 62.5 at 500. So the raise does not merely restore the old 57.1, it exceeds it; an earlier version of this entry printed ~58 for both ends and understated what 500 buys. ALL THREE OF THOSE ARE UPPER BOUNDS ON THE TRUE BREACH POINT, and the direction of the approximation is known rather than guessed: minPricedFraction gates on entryCostPriced, which is hitRate(field, e => Number.isFinite(e.entryCostSol)) — a share of FIELD ENTRANTS and not of launches. A launch skipped for budget is by construction one of the heaviest, so it carries more entrants than average and takes a larger share of the numerator than the launch-count arithmetic assumes, while every one of its entrants stays in the denominator. The entrant-weighted breach point therefore bites EARLIER than 57.1 / 50.0 / 62.5, and this repository holds no measured value for it — stated as an unmeasured optimistic gap rather than filled in with an invented figure. THE MEASURED MARGINS, so the number's provenance is honest rather than asserted. Replaying entryCostTargets as the code calls it over the committed tape (235 launches, 226 ten-launch windows) under stage2.mjs's greedy skip: the 400 ceiling was NEVER reached at either cap — 0 of 226 windows skipped a single launch — and the worst ten-launch window cost 350 of 400 against the worst eight-launch window's 316, i.e. headroom 84 at a cap of 8 falling to 50 at a cap of 10. WHY 500 DESPITE THE TAPE NEVER BREACHING 400, which is the captain's reasoning and is recorded as such: that margin evidence is n = 1 deployer while a full-day run screens STRANGERS, and the observed maximum of 74 transactions on a single launch already sits above the ~50 sustained breach point a cap of 10 at 400 would have created. An unmeasured cost is never a pass, so the failure this avoids is a NULL result rather than a false positive — but it is exactly the no-verdict outcome decision 190a exists to reduce, re-introduced on the busiest and therefore most gate-relevant candidates. An earlier version of this entry printed 200 / 380 / 700, which is the same arithmetic with the union left out (the plain sums 25 / 48 / 90 x 8); it overstated the cost by ~30% and the conclusion survives under either reading. The ceiling covers the median and the p90 whole and truncates only a pathological candidate, and it truncates VISIBLY: a launch is never priced half-way, so the ceiling costs whole launches and entry.coverage.cost records how many. THE NEW COST, stated here rather than discovered later: at the pinned 2.5s that is about 8 minutes per candidate at the median (190 requests at the cap of 10; it was ~6 at 152 requests under the cap of 8, and the ~8 an earlier version printed was the un-unioned 200) and about 21 at the ceiling, and at the maxCandidatesScored of 7 pinned on 2026-08-04 the declared worst case is 7 x 500 = 3,500 RPC requests and about 146 minutes (it read 3 x 500 = 1,500 and about 62.5 minutes at the scoring cap of 3, against 3 x 400 = 1,200 and about 50 minutes before this ceiling moved). The dry run prints it. The realistic cost is far lower because only candidates that survive room AND the gross field are priced at all — at the scoring cap of 3 the committed live run had one such candidate of three, and the same fraction at a cap of 7 is what a run actually pays.
justification.rpcMinIntervalMs: INHERITED FROM creation_walk.rpcMinIntervalMs AND NOT AN INDEPENDENT CHOICE — api.mainnet-beta rate-limits GLOBALLY across getSignaturesForAddress, getTransaction and getBlock, so this leg and the creation walk draw on one allowance. 2,500ms is that block's measured figure: 1,400ms is the documented floor but a 200-request run at that pace took over 890 seconds instead of 280 because the endpoint was shedding and the backoff was paying for it. The two legs are SERIALISED rather than run beside each other for the same reason: two concurrent jobs earned a sustained 429 lockout. Batching is not used here either — measured actively harmful on this host, 58s at batch=1 with zero shed events against 110s at batch=8 with eleven.
justification.preferBlockRoute: getBlock(slot, transactionDetails='full') returns EVERY transaction in the create slot in one request, collapsing the create-slot scope from ~7 requests a launch to 1. It is UNTESTED against this endpoint from this repo — what is known is that getBlock works here for signature listing; what is unknown is whether the public endpoint serves full blocks to this client and what a busy mainnet slot's payload costs. So it is probed BEHIND A FALLBACK: anything other than a usable block latches the candidate onto the per-signature route, and the route that ran reaches the run record so a saved run says which one paid for its numbers. It buys request count and NOTHING ELSE — in particular it does not reach out-of-transaction landing tips, because attributing a sibling transaction in the same slot to the same bundle is an inference the chain does not support. Set false to pin the walk to the proven route.

$comment: Hard bounds, enforced in code. There is no flag that disables one.
THE MADEONSOL ALLOWANCE HAS STOPPED BEING THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, AND THAT INVERSION IS WHAT
CAPTAIN DECISION 267a (2026-08-05) RE-SIZED THIS BLOCK AROUND. The key is now ULTRA and
EXCLUSIVE to slot-zero: `x-ratelimit-limit` 100,000/day, resetting at 00:00Z, read off the
wire 2026-08-05. It was ~200/day and shared, and every number here was derived from that 200 —
maxKeyedRequests WAS the daily allowance, and maxCandidates was what the allowance left after
enumeration and retries. At 100,000 exclusive a full run's keyed leg is 0.2% of a day, so an
allowance-derived ceiling would refuse nothing, and a ceiling that cannot refuse is not a
ceiling. Each value below is therefore RE-DERIVED from the constraint that actually binds it
now, and each justification names which one. Read them before quoting a figure here as an
allowance.
CAPTAIN'S INSTRUCTION, 2026-08-02, AND THE UPGRADE DOES NOT WIDEN IT: 'There is no current
free method to save on the madeonsol key request limits ... use all free tier daily quota as
needed if it gets results.' An earlier quarter-allowance ceiling of 45 was this tool's own
caution, never a captain instruction, and it is WITHDRAWN — do not reintroduce it or re-derive
it: there is no substitute for this data, so an unspent allowance buys nothing and only leaves
questions unanswered. But 267a re-derived these values against their REAL constraints and
raised nothing merely because the day got 500x bigger — maxCandidates is unchanged at 195 for
exactly that reason, and reading the Ultra upgrade as authorisation to widen a bound is a
captain decision this lane did not take.
WHAT NOTHING HERE CAN STILL SEE: the vendor sends x-ratelimit-limit / -remaining / -used /
-reset on EVERY response and no code in this repository reads one. These bounds govern ONE RUN

together — which is what stopped a run mid-flight on 2026-08-05, back when the day was 200 and
shared. At 100,000 exclusive that is no longer urgent; the GAP is unchanged. Read the header
before a multi-leg session.
The conditional binds: 'if it gets results'. This authorises sizing a run by what the
question needs. It does NOT authorise sweeping, idle retrying, or re-running to re-evidence a

allowance.
SCOPE: this relaxation is MadeOnSol ONLY. The SolanaTracker / CoinGecko keys are shared with

unchanged, as is the keyless pump.fun pacing below, which bounds a shared public resource for
an entirely different reason.

this research lane alone, so the whole 10M monthly allowance is this tool's and no other
consumer can be starved by a heavy run. It is metered on its own terms in
creation_walk_helius, in CREDITS rather than requests, because that is what the vendor bills.
The MadeOnSol burst limit WAS the one thing the 2026-08-02 relaxation did not touch: ~10/min
was recorded as a rate the vendor enforced rather than our own caution, so keyedMinIntervalMs
stayed. Decision 267a required it to be RE-MEASURED on Ultra instead of carried across, and
